title: Alexander and Porus: the Hydaspes
deck: A river crossing in a storm, an army of war elephants, and a defeated king who kept his throne.
confidenceNote: High — well attested; exact site debated

facts.label: OUTCOME
facts.value: Macedonian victory; Porus kept his kingdom

chapters.heading: Alexander reaches the Indus
chapters.body: In 327–326 BCE Alexander's army crossed the Hindu Kush and the Indus. Local rulers such as Ambhi of Taxila chose to ally with him.

chapters.heading: Porus holds the river
chapters.body: Porus, king of the Paurava realm, held the far bank of the Hydaspes (Jhelum) with infantry, chariots and war elephants.

chapters.heading: The crossing
chapters.body: According to Arrian, Alexander left part of his force at the main camp and crossed upstream by night during a storm.

chapters.heading: The battle
chapters.body: Alexander's cavalry outflanked Porus's army. The elephants panicked and trampled their own side, and the Indian army was defeated.

chapters.heading: A king who kept his throne
chapters.body: Alexander reinstated Porus as a ruler and ally. Soon after, at the Hyphasis (Beas), his army refused to march further east.

keyIdea.text: The ancient accounts agree on the outcome, but historians still debate the exact crossing point on the Jhelum.
